method: Whole XAML and code-behind reading; pinned Git blob identities verified. No tray/hook/registry actions executed.
findings: Tray state XAML bindings are OneTime; subsequent state updates rely on imperative commands rather than observable settings synchronization.
Dispose only disposes TrayIcon; three HookManager event subscriptions remain attached and queued dispatcher work has no disposed guard or cancellation.
Shell-initialization callback loops helper for seven seconds when icon hidden and posts dispatcher updates; timing and callback-thread blocking require runtime qualification.
Hook toggle writes persistent setting before starting/stopping hook and does not rollback if action throws, allowing requested state to diverge from actual hook status.
Reuse-tabs command ensures window hook enabled, and disabling window hook disables reuse-tabs. Shortcut restoration uses a saved boolean rather than independent state transaction.

ToggleHookState assumes at least one profile when enabling keyboard/mouse menu and none checked, then accesses Items[0]. RelayCommand CanExecute guards HasItems for normal command routing but direct Execute calls do not enforce that predicate; actual empty-list reachability needs caller validation.
Profile submenu objects retain mutable profile references; enabling updates ProfileManager directly. No file-content comparison is implemented by reuse-tabs option.
limits: Static review only; no reproduced tray race or runtime failure. Third-party TaskbarIcon implementation remains outside this repository source scope.
